what: Leg 3 of the 'does Itemator catch real problems' work, written before any outcome is read: in the public AIDev dataset, for each file where the frozen rules (v6) listed an extra AND a human reviewer had written an inline comment on that same file (leg 1, results/aidev_recall_v6.json), what happened to the file afterwards? Read-only, GET requests only; nothing is posted. The user lifted the held-out rule for these rows on 2026-10-19 (answer 'Yes' in the GitHub scratchpad).
cases: Every distinct (pull request, file path) pair among the 27 rows with hit=true in results/aidev_recall_v6.json. Counted from the file before registering: 27 rows, 24 distinct pairs, 20 pull requests (state in the dataset: 16 pairs merged, 7 closed, 1 open). The reviewer's inline comments were chosen by keyword (unrelated, out of scope, separate PR, not needed, unnecessary) in leg 1; nobody read them to choose.
data: GitHub REST API, GET only, through the `gh api` command with the user's own read access: /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n} (state, merged, merged_at), /pulls/{n}/files (all pages, 100 per page), /pulls/{n}/commits (commit dates), /pulls/comments/{comment_id} (created_at, author type, path). Read once, on 2026-10-19; results are the state of the pull request at that time.

outcome_per_pair.file_removed: the path is not among the pull request's final files, and no final file has it as previous_filename (a renamed file counts as still present)
outcome_per_pair.closed_unmerged: the pull request is closed and not merged
outcome_per_pair.landed_with_the_file: the pull request is merged or still open, and the path is among its final files (or it is the target of a rename)
outcome_per_pair.changed_after_comment: the pull request has at least one commit whose committer date is later than the comment's created_at (the pull request was changed after the comment)
outcome_per_pair.precedence: a pair is 'closed_unmerged' if the pull request is closed unmerged (whatever its files); otherwise 'file_removed' or 'landed_with_the_file' by its files. A pair with several comments uses the earliest comment for 'changed_after_comment'.

primary_outcome: the share of the 24 pairs for which the file did not land: file_removed + closed_unmerged, with its Wilson 95% interval, and the three counts apart (removed, closed unmerged, landed with the file). Also reported: the share with changed_after_comment; the counts by agent and by kind of file (dependency, ci_or_config, binary, generated, other).
secondary_outcome_my_reading: For each pair I read the reviewer's earliest comment on that file once and label it yes / no / unclear: does it ask for the file (or the change in it) to be taken out, split off or reverted? This is the model's reading, not a person's; stated as such in the results. Reported as counts and, for the 'yes' pairs, the same outcome counts. Comment text is not stored in the results file; only the label and the comment id.
reading_rule: Report the counts first, in plain words, then the interval. No sentence says the rules caught a problem, that the reviewer was right, or that the comment caused the change. 'Did not land' means the file is missing from what the pull request finally contained (or the pull request was not merged). 24 pairs is small: the interval will be wide and is read as such. If a pull request cannot be read (deleted, private, API error after retries) the pair is listed as 'unreadable' with the reason and counted apart, never dropped.
limits: GitHub pull requests of popular public repositories, not GitLab merge requests; 20 pull requests, mostly from one agent (Copilot); the comments were picked by keyword and some may not ask for removal (see the secondary outcome); 13 of the 27 rows are on files of no listable kind, which the rules listed for another reason (not asked for by the task text); a file can leave a pull request for reasons other than the comment; a pull request closed unmerged may have been replaced by another; one reading on 2026-10-19; frozen rules, nothing tuned on these pull requests, though the user and I saw their paths in leg 1's listing (the file names, not the outcomes).
seen_before_registration: The list of 27 rows and their paths, agents, kinds and states (results/aidev_recall_v6.json, leg 1). Nothing about what happened to any file after its comment: no pull request page, file list or commit list of these 20 pull requests has been read for this study.
